text:
maria: Trying to spin up a dense GPU nodepool in us-west3 for the batch-inference fleet and it immediately failed with IP quota errors when creating nodes. Anyone run into this when trying to pack many pods per GPU?
aj: What did the gcloud output look like and which cluster?
maria: cluster: gpu-serving-west3, command was trying 16 nodes with --max-pods-per-node=120. Error: 
```
ERROR: (gcloud.container.node_pools.create) ResponseError: code=409, message=Failed to create nodepool: failedPrecondition: secondary range "pods-us-west3" does not have enough free IP addresses to create node(s).
Caused by: Quota 'IN_USE_ADDRESSES' exceeded.
```
Looks like the cluster's pods secondary range was small (it was /26 at creation).
oliver: Yup, this is the alias-IP / secondary range issue. For VPC-native clusters GKE allocates one IP per pod from the secondary range. So required capacity ~= nodes * maxPodsPerNode + headroom. A /26 only gives ~60 addresses, so you'll hit it fast.
sre-ops: Two approaches: expand the subnet's secondary range (add a larger CIDR) OR reduce max-pods-per-node and allow more nodes. Also open a GCP quota ticket for IN_USE_ADDRESSES if you're near project limits.
networking: Expanding a secondary range is possible but needs care: check for overlapping CIDRs and peering constraints. If the subnet was created by infra templates we need change approval (NET-2026-089). We should also confirm there are no /32 reservations in the range.
cloud-accounts: We can file quota increases. For us-west3 please confirm exact GPU SKU (A100 vs A100 v4). Quotas to request: IN_USE_ADDRESSES (regional), and Accelerators: "NVIDIA A100" for the region. Provide project ID and target counts.
maria: Project: redwood-inference-prod, region: us-west3, GPUs requested: 64 (8 nodes x 8 gpus), SKU: nvidia-a100. Secondary range name: pods-us-west3 currently /26.
aj: While quota requests are pending, the quick workaround is to create an interim node pool with a lower max-pods-per-node so the secondary range fits current capacity. Example we used elsewhere: 
```
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-dense-temp \
  --cluster=gpu-serving-west3 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100,count=8 \
  --num-nodes=4 \
  --max-pods-per-node=32 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=2 --max-nodes=24
```
That reduces immediate address consumption and lets autoscaler scale out as more pods are scheduled.
oliver: Another medium-term option is to create a new subnet with a larger pods secondary range (eg /22 or /20 depending on projected scale) and create a new cluster or use node auto-provisioning across subnets. Expanding the existing secondary range to /22 is possible in many cases but must be coordinated with network owners.
kubernetes-team: Note: changing max-pods-per-node is a node-pool property — you cannot change it on existing nodes without recreating the pool. Also beware that reducing max-pods-per-node increases number of nodes which increases VM overhead and scheduling latency. Consider affinity and topology spread to keep GPU utilization high.
sre-ops: For cost/perf tradeoffs: if your pods are tiny CPU-lite and GPU-bound, more VMs means more idle CPU/memory overhead but you keep GPUs busy. If pods are extremely small it's worth exploring GPU MPS / MIG or multi-instance GPU to serve multiple models per GPU without spawning many pods. Check runtime compatibility with A100 and MIG.
cloud-accounts: I've opened CLOUD-2026-215 (GCP quotas: IN_USE_ADDRESSES + nvidia-a100 in us-west3) and NET-2026-090 (request to expand secondary range on subnet inference-subnet-us-west3). Adding justification: high-density batch inference for SLA-bound customers.
infra-bot: Created ticket CLOUD-2026-215 assigned to cloud-accounts. Created ticket NET-2026-090 assigned to networking.
maria: Quick ask on the quota ticket: do we also need "Alias IP ranges per subnet" quota bumped or is IN_USE_ADDRESSES enough?
cloud-accounts: IN_USE_ADDRESSES is the blocker for immediate creation. If the project has hard limits on alias ranges you may need that too — we'll include both in the request.
oliver: Short-term alternatives if quota expansion drags: 1) provision in a nearby region (us-west2) where we have spare IP/GPU quota; 2) use preemptible instances to reduce cost and spread load; 3) split the workload across multiple smaller clusters. All have pros/cons.
sre-ops: If you go multi-region, ensure model weights and cache priming are handled to avoid cold-starts. Also update smart-routing policies (we have a route config) to failover gracefully.
maria: I spun up the interim pool with --max-pods-per-node=32 and 4 nodes, pods are scheduling now. Will monitor 99p latency and GPU saturation. Please update tickets when quotas/secondary range changes progress.
networking: We're evaluating expansion options and will post NET-2026-090 updates here when we have a time window. Might require a brief maintenance window if route changes are needed.
aj: Action items recap: cloud-accounts to push quotas (CLOUD-2026-215), networking to evaluate secondary-range expansion (NET-2026-090), infra to validate interim pool and test autoscaler behavior, infra/research to evaluate MIG or multi-tenant GPU strategies.
maria: Thanks all — ping me on the ticket when the subnet range is expanded so we can create the final high-density pool.
